author: Autodesk
description: This graph generates a field of grass, waving in the wind
documentation:
## Grass Wind

### `What it Does`
This graph both generates strand-based grass and a field to simulate a wind blowing through the grass.  This graph is not physically accurate in terms of inter-strand collisions, but does offer a good simulacrum of the effect.

### `How it works`
The blade generator node is essentially a loop that generates n instances of grass blades, it is built upon a very basic quadratic bezier curve and includes options for bending, height, strand resolution and strand profile curve.  This allows you to build n unique instances that are then instances onto a point object.  Once the scattering is complete and bakes, the graph only computes on the first frame and the resulting bake is deformed by a wind field which is generated by combining fields and noises to achieve the desired look.  The "stiffness" of the grass is achieved by multiplying the wind field by the point ratio of the strands, which run from zero at the bottom to 1 at the top, including an fCurve for adjustment.

### `Settings`
***Blade Generator***
*bend_x_min* and *bend_x_max*:  How much bend in the blade's x direction, random per instance.
*bend_z_min* and *bend_z_max*:  How much bend in the blade's z direction, random per instance.
*height_min* and *height_max*:  Minimum and Maximum blade heights, random per instance.
*min_bend_position* and *max_bend_position*:  Where the middle point of the 3 point curve is along the length of the blade, random per instance.
*min_width* and *max_width*:  Minimum and Maximum blade width, random per instance.
*number of blades*:  The number of instances generated.
*blade_resolution*:  How many points in each blade strand.
*blade_profile_curves*:  An array of fCurves to randomly choose a blade's size profile.

***adjust_grass_stiffness***
*adjust_strands*:  This fCurve controls the interpretation of the point_ratio property from the root to the tip of the blade.
*grass_color*:  Controls the color of the strands.

***apply_wind_field***
*wind_speed*:  How fast the wind moves.
*wind_strength*:  How strong the wind force is.
*wind_direction*:  A vector value controlling the major direction of the wind field.  NB:  Only x and z values are taken into account.

The output of this graph is the moving strands as an object.  This can be rendered directly in Arnold utilising *set_Arnold_strands_settings*.

_notes.text:
# instancing

Create, bake and cache the instances.  The ***compute_on_frame*** compound acts as a cache, baking the instances **only** on the frame specified.  This is what enables the speed of this graph.

# adjustment and wind field

Adjust the stiffness property (*point_ratio*) on the strands and meshes, create and apply the wind field, with custom settings.
Vertex color can also be set here - the strands are colored using this, multiplied by their *point_ratio* property.  This provides a handy visual guide in the viewport.

This is the geo to scatter on.
Feel free to plug in your own here.

# master scatter

The master scattering setup.  The "blades"  will be instanced on these points.  

*point_scale* and *point_orientation* are set here by the two random compounds.

# instance generator

This section generates blades of grass using a simple bezier curve generator.  The interior loop enables random generation of any number of unique instances to be fed into the point-instancer.

_notes.text: This section controls how the blade looks along the strand.
